en:
<style=AlmParagraph>Drafting & Combat
</style>- To control your settlers directly, draft them by selecting them, and clicking on the draft action in their selection panel. 
- A drafted settler will go where you tell them to go and will attack who you tell them to attack.
- During combat an archer will shoot anybody within their range, while a melee settler will wait until the enemy comes close or attacks them. <style=AlmParagraph>
Tip
</style><style=Desc>- Place archers on higher ground in order for them to get a buff in precision, range, and critical hit chance.</style>

en: Job Priorities - The JOB panel is where you can prioritize each settler's tasks. - By default, settlers will prioritize their jobs from left to right. - Using and , you can change job priorities so that a given settler will choose one job before another. - Jobs set to the same priority level will be prioritized left to right. - If the job box is empty, that means that a settler will never do that job. - Settlers will always do the highest priority job that they can find. - If a specific job is not on anyone's priority list, that job will never get done. - The frame colour of a job box indicates the settler's skill level. Tip - If a settler has a very low skill rating for a specific job, it is better to turn that job off completely for that settler - otherwise, there is a chance they'll do the job and fail. This is important when it comes to things like harvesting. Example: a settler with a low botanical skill level could end up ruining the harvest, yielding no resources. So it's best to let them focus on what they do best!

en:
<style=AlmParagraph>Mood
</style>- Mood represents your settlers' happiness.
- Be sure to check on your settlers’ mood often.
- A low mood can result in settlers rebelling and refusing to follow orders.
- If a settler's mood reaches 0, they will leave your settlement.
- Things like cooked or lavish meals, comfortable beds, and a fair amount of leisure time can help keep your settlers’ spirits high.

en:
<style=AlmParagraph>Bartering
</style>- Bartering functions by exchanging resources and items with a Merchant.
- You can request resources only if you proffer something in return with the same or similar value.
- The settler making the trade can influence prices, and can also negotiate to get more than they offered.

- Giving the merchant more value than is received will be considered a gift, and will influence alignment favourably towards the Merchant's faction.
- The value of resources is determined by merchant type, faction, alignment, and even time of year.

<style=AlmParagraph>Relocate Structures
</style>- Smaller structures like furniture, workstations and decorations can be easily relocated: Select an already-constructed structure and click on the relocate button. Then select a new location.

- Structures that are removed will turn into a resource pile and can be stored on stockpiles, and even traded with Merchants.

en:
<style=AlmParagraph>Farming
</style>- Sow crop fields to ensure a steady supply of food for the upcoming winter. 
- Choose a crop from the zone panel [<style=Shortcut>F7</style>], then drag it to the required size.
- You need appropriate supplies of seeds and saplings in order to sow.
- New varieties of crop fields will be unlocked as you acquire new seed types, either by foraging, or from merchants. 
- Remember that plants need sunlight. Sow crops in the open, away from trees or structures that will create shade. Days are shorter in winter and early spring, so try to avoid sowing plants during this time.

en: Animals Wild Animals - Settlers can hunt and butcher wild animals for meat and leather. - Some animals like wolves and boars have a chance to retaliate when hunted. - To hunt an animal, a settler needs to be equipped with a ranged weapon. Domestic Animals - Some wild animals can be tamed. - Some animals may attack a settler who is trying to tame them, so beware. -Taming can be a long process and can't be done continually. Settlers can try to tame an animal once every 24h. - Tamed animals will live alongside settlers. Some animals can be kept in animal pens. To create a pen, place a pen marker in a fenced off or enclosed area. Pets - Some domestic animals can be trained to become pets. - Pets can be assigned to settlers so that they will follow them around and even help out around the settlement.

en: Each settler has a story about the past they left far behind. But now, this tattered group has a common goal: to build a new home, together.

en: The plague had ravaged the British Isles, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. Untold millions went to an early grave. And those left standing were plunged into poverty, brutally scarred by the horrors that they had witnessed. Nothing would ever be the same again.\n\n<season_description> of the year <year>, <all_villagers> set off into the wilderness to claim a piece of the land as their own, as was their right, in the eyes of God and under the Law. Here, they may lay down the foundations for some kind of future. Perhaps hope will follow.

en: <random_villager> surveys the half-starved group, and states the obvious. 'We're not exactly on fighting form, are we?' Why go looking for a fight, [he/she] thinks, when we could strive to create a cosy, welcoming hearth?

en: [He/She] stands before them, legs planted wide. 'We have fought before...we all bear the scars.' The travellers nod in unison. Each of them has been tougher than they ever thought possible, in these plague years. <random_villager> speaks quietly. They lean forward. 'Nobody will ever rip us from our stronghold. We shall build it, and defend it.' Then [he/she] roars: 'By the Devil, let them try!'

en:
The starting narrative will appear in the historical records as well as the loading screen. Using special elements like:
<village_name> will insert the name of your settlement in the text
<year> Will insert the starting year in your text
<all_villagers> will insert all settler names in the format: "John, Jack and Merry"
